    <h1>When the vacuum becomes a prism</h1>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
Renormalization is sometimes seen as a formal trick. Yet it uncovers a new layer of reality with real physical effects. One of them is the **birefringence of the vacuum** in a strong electromagnetic field, which follows from the Lagrangian of Euler and Heisenberg [\[1\]](#ref-1). In this project you will see that quantum fluctuations make the vacuum an optically anisotropic medium.

- In classical electrodynamics the Lagrangian of the field is $$L_0 = \frac{1}{8\pi}(\boldsymbol{E}^2 - \boldsymbol{B}^2).$$ Quantum corrections due to virtual electron--positron pairs lead to nonlinear effects. At low energies the effective Lagrangian (the Euler--Heisenberg Lagrangian) takes the form $$L_{\text{eff}} = L_0 + \frac{e^4}{360\pi^2 m_e^4} \left[(\boldsymbol{E}^2 - \boldsymbol{B}^2)^2 + 7(\boldsymbol{E} \cdot \boldsymbol{B})^2\right].$$

  (a) Derive the expressions for the displacement and the magnetizing field: $$\boldsymbol{D} = 4\pi \frac{\partial L_{\text{eff}}}{\partial \boldsymbol{E}}, \quad \boldsymbol{H} = -4\pi \frac{\partial L_{\text{eff}}}{\partial \boldsymbol{B}}.$$

  (b) Compare the constitutive relations you obtain with those of the vacuum. What has changed?

- Linearize the equations, assuming that the field consists of a background $\boldsymbol{E}_0, \boldsymbol{B}_0$ and a small perturbation $\delta \boldsymbol{E}, \delta \boldsymbol{B}$. Obtain the permittivity and permeability tensors of the medium.

- Write Maxwell's equations for the wave perturbation. Find the dispersion relation for a wave propagating along the $x$ axis, assuming that the constant magnetic field is directed along the $z$ axis: $$\boldsymbol{B}_0 = B_0 \boldsymbol{e}_z.$$

- Consider two cases:

  (a) the electric field of the wave is parallel to $\boldsymbol{B}_0$ (polarization along the $z$ axis);

  (b) the electric field of the wave is perpendicular to $\boldsymbol{B}_0$ (polarization along the $y$ axis).

  ✓  Find the refractive indices $n_\parallel$ and $n_\perp$ and their difference $$\Delta n = n_\parallel - n_\perp.$$

- Propose an experiment to observe vacuum birefringence. Which effect could be used: interference, rotation of the polarization, a phase shift? What fields and what sensitivity are needed?

## References

[1]{#ref-1} Heisenberg, Werner, Euler, Hans, *Consequences of Dirac's theory of the positron*, Zeitschrift für Physik **98** 714–732 (1936) <https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01343663>
